name: dual-llm-quarantine
context: Agent systems exposed to untrusted input (user prompts, fetched web pages, email attachments, third-party API responses) that may contain prompt injection attacks. A Privileged LLM holds tool access but never sees raw untrusted content; a Quarantined LLM processes untrusted data and returns only typed structured extractions. The two communicate through opaque handles — the Privileged LLM composes tool calls using these handles without ever observing the raw content that triggered the injection.
benefits: Strong defense against prompt injection attacks
No single execution path holds all three: private data, untrusted content, outbound channel
Works without modifying the underlying model
tradeoffs: Near-doubled cost and latency (two LLM calls per processing step)
Requires a privileged LLM that never sees untrusted content
Symbolic handle design needs careful schema specification
Does not prevent injection in the user prompt itself
use_cases: Email assistants that read inbound messages and draft replies
Web research agents that browse untrusted pages
CRM systems processing inbound customer messages with tool access
Document processing pipelines with tool execution
avoid_when: All input is fully trusted (internal tools only)
anti_patterns: Letting the Privileged LLM ever see raw untrusted content
Free-form text responses from the Quarantined LLM
No schema validation on structured extractions
design_principles: Zero-content exposure: Privileged LLM sees handles only, never raw untrusted data
Fail-closed on schema validation: reject malformed extractions from Quarantined LLM
Least privilege on tool access: tools available only to Privileged LLM
best_practices: Define minimal schemas for each extraction task (30-char max field names)
Rate-limit or timeout the Quarantined LLM to prevent resource exhaustion
Log all Quarantined LLM extractions for audit trail
references: Willison, The Dual LLM Pattern for Building AI Assistants that Resist Prompt Injection, 2023 — https://simonwillison.net/2023/Apr/14/dual-llm-pattern/
Beurer-Kellner et al., Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections, 2025 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08837
Debenedetti et al., Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL), 2025 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813
